_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Abu Dhabi v3 fleet-investors structure per the international addendum (UAE run — tourism-weighted utilization stack; RAK is the resort/experience play, deployment timed to the destination's published build-out). Sources: ras-al-khaimah/REVENUE-STACK-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md + CREW-COST-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md + TOURISM-DEMAND-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md + SPEED-RULES-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md. GEOMETRY-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.json is NOT a content source — the sealed RAK set is contaminated (mis-geocoded Dubai/AD POIs) and is cited only as the contamination finding for Grok locale cleanup (#119). NO route_ids render or bind anywhere in this file; the network is the four journey-spine corridors with DERIVED-approximate distances (Al Marjan↔Al Hamra 4.0 nm · Mina Al Arab↔Corniche 10.0 · Al Marjan↔Corniche 17.0 · Creek↔Jazirat Al Hamra 13.0). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. Fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty firewalls apply in full. Parent-approved framing: honest headline is the MID case ~11.7-yr payback rendered without apology; the ~3.5-yr case renders only as a clearly labeled conditional (Al Marjan resort cluster open — Wynn, Sept 2027); the conservative case renders cash-negative (−$1,912/mo) plainly. Calm frame: capital follows the destination's published growth (1.35M→3.5M visitors by 2030, $5.1B Wynn opening 2027) — no demand-gated-launch mechanics language. All scenario figures transcribed exactly from the worked revenue model and re-verified by script before writing. Demand pools are sourced visitor/development flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists (international addendum). No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced RAK fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders.

fn1.text: Experience and charter pricing is positioned against Ras Al Khaimah's sourced water-leisure market: pearl-farm tours published at US$50–71 per person, mangrove kayaking at AED 100–175, the authority's heritage water line renting craft at AED 150 per 30 minutes and AED 300 per hour, and the AED 325 zipline as the emirate's marquee activity price. Published hourly charter rates above the heritage-craft tier are thin, so the charter band is a derived range with a conservative haircut.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced visitor flows and published development facts, not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: Ras Al Khaimah publishes no numeric waterway speed limits today. Every trip time on this page uses a conservative planning basis — slow near berths, in the creek and in the lagoons, 25 knots on the open coast, 20 knots after dark — and corridor distances are approximate, computed from real coordinates with over-water routing factors and rounded up. Final schedules are set with the transport authority under its 2026 marine regulation. The water line is never sold as faster than the road.

fn5.text: Committed-seat and spot pricing is a derived band, not a Ras Al Khaimah quote: anchored to the published street-taxi tariff, metered fares on these corridors, and a road-commute anchor of about AED 2,508 a month for Al Marjan to the city. Roads here are largely free-flowing, so pricing is positioned on arrival experience and direct resort-to-city hops, not time savings. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a UAE-adapted method: published UAE maritime wage surveys for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), plus explicitly stated housing, transport, end-of-service, visa and medical allowances. The model uses $30 per hour loaded — the mid benchmark rounded up as a buffer. No emirate-specific wage rows were found, so UAE-wide benchmarks are used and labeled.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: The conservative case is cash-negative: on a deliberately thin month before the 2027 resort openings, fixed costs exceed what one vessel earns. It is shown plainly as the floor — not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year on a sheltered southern Gulf coast. June–September heat shifts midday sailings toward morning and evening slots; October–April is the event-season peak. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with that shape absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at the published commercial electricity tariff for the northern emirates plus VAT — about $0.123 per kWh, applied at the top consumption slab to every kilowatt-hour as a conservative reading. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line rises about 2.4×; the mid case stays cash-positive with payback moving to roughly 13.3 years.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Local benchmarks are cited in UAE dirhams and convert at the pegged rate of 3.6725 dirhams per dollar.

fn12.text: Al Marjan Island has no public marine facility verified today. Its stop renders with that status stated: an interim landing coordinated through the operating yacht club's moorings, with the published Wynn Al Marjan marina (opening 2027) as the permanent landing.

fn13.text: Mina Al Arab's marina is developer-published and not independently verified as an operating facility; the Anantara resort on the lagoon operates today. The Jazirat Al Hamra waterfront has no verified marine facility and renders as a heritage-shore stop with that status stated.

copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in a fraction of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day, twelve months a year. In Ras Al Khaimah the stack is deliberately experience-led: resort transfers, tourism sailings and charters carry the working case, committed seats stay small until the 2027 resort wave lands, and the numbers are shown plainly — including a cash-negative floor.

Weakest-anchored price in this file — flagged.
layer_pricing_basis.sponsorship_U1: $150K/yr fleet-level placeholder ÷ 4 vessels = $3,125/mo, program precedent. Upside only.
layer_pricing_basis.overnight_cargo_U2: 12 runs × $250 — courier-linehaul rate logic; no RAK waterborne freight tariff found ⇒ upside-only. Clean classes per the stack: resort resupply (Al Marjan/Al Hamra/Mina Al Arab), premium parcels, medical/lab specimens.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.
